# dlanhs

> Returns the value of the one norm, Frobenius norm, infinity norm, or the largest absolute value of a real upper Hessenberg matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlanhs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlanhs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlanhs( order, norm, N, A, LDA, WORK ) → number
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `norm` | `("one-norm"\|"max"\|"inf-norm"\|"frobenius")` | in |  |  | `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in | `max( N, 1 ) × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `A` |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out |  |  | workspace array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in DLANHS as described above.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, DLANHS is set to zero.
- `A`: The n by n upper Hessenberg matrix A; the part of A below the first sub-diagonal is not referenced.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'`; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: matrix norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlanhs.ndarray(
    norm,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → number
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `("one-norm"\|"max"\|"inf-norm"\|"frobenius")` | in |  |  | `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in | `max( N, 1 ) × N` |  | upper Hessenberg matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `A` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | workspace array (length >= N, used for `'inf-norm'` only) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in DLANHS as described above.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, DLANHS is set to zero.
- `A`: The n by n upper Hessenberg matrix A; the part of A below the first sub-diagonal is not referenced.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'`; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: matrix norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlanhs()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLANHS`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlanhs.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlanhs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlanhs';

// 3x3 upper Hessenberg matrix (column-major, LDA=3):

// A = [ 1  2  3 ]

//     [ 4  5  6 ]

//     [ 0  7  8 ]
const A = new Float64Array([
	1.0,
	4.0,
	0.0,
	2.0,
	5.0,
	7.0,
	3.0,
	6.0,
	8.0
]);
const WORK = new Float64Array( 3 );

// Max norm: largest absolute value
const maxNorm = dlanhs( 'column-major', 'max', 3, A, 3, WORK );
console.log( 'Max norm: %d', maxNorm ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => Max norm: 8

// One norm: maximum column sum
const oneNorm = dlanhs( 'column-major', 'one-norm', 3, A, 3, WORK );
console.log( 'One norm: %d', oneNorm ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => One norm: 17

// Infinity norm: maximum row sum
const infNorm = dlanhs( 'column-major', 'inf-norm', 3, A, 3, WORK );
console.log( 'Infinity norm: %d', infNorm ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => Infinity norm: 15

// Frobenius norm: sqrt of sum of squares
const frobNorm = dlanhs( 'column-major', 'frobenius', 3, A, 3, WORK );
console.log( 'Frobenius norm: %d', frobNorm ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => Frobenius norm: 14.2828568570857
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLANHS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLANHS returns the value of the one norm, or the Frobenius norm, or the infinity norm, or the element of largest absolute value of a Hessenberg matrix A.

### Returns

$$
\mathrm{DLANHS} = \begin{cases} \max (\lvert A(i,j) \rvert) & \text{NORM = 'M' or 'm'} \\ \mathrm{norm1}(A) & \text{NORM = '1', 'O' or 'o'} \\ \mathrm{normI}(A) & \text{NORM = 'I' or 'i'} \\ \mathrm{normF}(A) & \text{NORM = 'F', 'f', 'E' or 'e'} \end{cases}
$$

where norm1 denotes the one norm of a matrix (maximum column sum), normI denotes the infinity norm of a matrix (maximum row sum) and normF denotes the Frobenius norm of a matrix (square root of sum of squares). Note that max(abs(`A(i,j)`)) is not a consistent matrix norm.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
